[quote=camphill;60234431][b]Expansion Post[/b]

Camphill for its entire history has stayed in 1 place, northern Vespuria. Since camphill's monarchy became constitutional, we stayed in Northern Vespuria. Since we combined our monarchy with [nation]Akhratia[/nation]s, we've stayed in one place. But now, we will expand, we will move into former Anrakan Land and take over, It is time for camphill to grow! 

"Peace is, much better then killing people, I assumed the press knew that." -Alexander Arramont, former king of Camphill.... There is a reason Alexander is dead, he was weak, he stayed in one country his entire life, he hated war and pain too much, well by today's government standards. He was pathetic, he was a weak ruler, he was a coward.

But our new leader, our young Queen and Empress, is daring and strong. She has the strength to conquer, to take over, and to move. She is a bright young mind, and has plenty of time to do as she likes.

The conservative government in camphill has won the election for its second time in a row. Our empress and the government has teamed up to expand camphill land area and population. Though the population of camphill is used to being at peace for most of its history. They will riot and break things, and make a lot of noise. But our government must get though it for the future of camphill. 

Ljaná the 3rd's speech to the people "People of Camphill, congrats on the Conservatives for winning the presidential election. I support the government for any policies they will have. Now everyone, we must do our best for camphill to prosper."

[pre]下界  Xiàjiè. The world beneath the world. There is no ambiguity in the definition, there is a world beneath the surface of the lake. The voice is there because it wants for us to meet her, but everyday we fail to find it. Every day she gives her grand performance at the abyss of water. We have the means, do we not? With these great machines we can explore the absolute depths of clarity and meet the source of all the world's beauty. Why do we not strive for it? Why do we not search for it?[/pre]

[spoiler=The World Beneath the World]

[b]The World Beneath the World[/b]

Some people flaunt the size of their universities. 

"It's like its own city!" You might hear your friend remarking to you after his first day, excited to explain to you in detail the rows of buildings, each functioning independent of the other, with their own offices and staff, faculty that hardly ever of one another due to the sheer scale of their operations. They might talk about the open space and the beauty that surrounded them, or perhaps the multitude of people's organizations, each with their own defined science or sector, the camaraderie manifest in their ranks, and the events that seemingly appear in various parts of the university.

However, have you ever seen a university that was its own country? A university so great, so immense, that its faculty managed itself not in buildings nor in groups of buildings but instead according to internal borders? A university that sustained itself so well that it had no need of shopping malls or electronic stores, rather manufacturing plants that provided all of the student body's needs at great discount. Where livestock are grown, fattened, slaughtered, prepared, and cooked all within the colleges themselves, all handled by a Faculty of Agriculture? Where the Faculty of Medicine is tasked not only with teaching pregnancy but with directing labor and birth within their very own hospital?

Have you ever seen a university that had its own tax collectors and armed forces? What about its own religion?

[list]

"Hell no." Cui Jin loudly reacted, his eyebrows furrowing as he glanced carefully towards the small platoon of Red Guards marching along the front entrance of one of the university buildings. "I knew that the 661 Campus was very independent, but this is basically political separation."

"Don't get things twisted, Comrade Cui. The University remains committed to the principles of the Qianxun Socialist Republic and the MZP." Zhang Meihui assures, pulling Cui along by the shoulder to focus on their walk. "Besides, why are you complaining? You're going to be our party secretary now. You'd be the leader of your own place. Wouldn't that be nice?"

"It makes me anxious. Have you ever been free? Makes a man feel sick."

"Best lose that thought process when you're in the university, Comrade Cui. It's not going to grant you any favors."

[/list]

The two turned around a street sign and made their way through yet another, smaller white granite gate. Through it, a massive lawn and beautiful path leading into the Campus Registrar, its building designed in the style of the wooden halls of ancient Qianxun history, but encased in sturdier rock and glass. The pair queued for the first desk on bureaucratic matters, and Cui Jin greeted the registrar, who took merely a second to confirm his military uniform before immediately bowing down and acceding to his every demand. Staff ID? Education license? Employment papers? All were given to him in a single meet what would take most men at least a week, as though they've been prepared in advance.

[list]

"You're quite popular, Comrade Cui." Zhang said in passing as they walked out of the Registrar and towards one of the waiting e-taxis.

"My uncle is popular." Cui responds. "Though it does help my life a bit."

"You have a good relationship with your uncle?"

"Good enough to grant me a nice job I guess."

[/list]

Like a lot of UQ's public utility, the e-taxi is driverless, programmed to go through preprogrammed routes. As the pair enter, the vehicle began advancing along the road leading to the heart of the university. Form gives way to function as the signs pass them by, whispering to them that they now approached something greater than themselves. They were approaching one of the Qianxun Lakes, Lake Qianxun Major.

In place of white granite or marble was solid concrete and steel like those in the exterior walls. And not only that, fences rose up, the number of students seen prancing about quadrupled, roads began parting in more and more directions, and at the center stage it was there with a shiny blue face. Lake Qianxun Major. It was around 300 kilometers in length and twice as much in width, perfectly clear, with no single mat of water hyacinth or algal bloom emanating out of its surface, not even a semblance of human tarnishing across its coastal sands despite the seemingly endless array of research stations perched up upon its rocks and waters.

[list]

"Welcome to Qianxun Major, Comrade Cui." Zhang introduced as the e-taxi halted and shut down. "Just like in the photos?"

"Even better than the photos." Cui admitted, taking a moment to bask in the view. "... But, I've also heard of many rumors about this place. Fearful rumors. My uncle says that your last party secretary became mad."

"The beauty of rumors is that you do not need to believe them."

[/list]

As they exit, the e-taxi reactivates and drives off. Then, Zhang Meihui walks over to the building they had stopped at. It was a residential building, like a traditional siheyuan, with a great courtyard enclosed on all sides by a network of interlocking buildings arranged into a neat rectangle. At the front of the building was the symbol of the Min Zhu Party, waiting patiently for its next occupant to come meet its amenities. And yet, it was not someone's palace. It was definitely not a residence, for it was too large and brazen, too ostentatious in its luxury to be tolerable to Qianxun's socialist society. 

[list]

"This is...?"

"The [i]yamen[/i]." Zhang says, pointing to the front door with its card reader. "Or at least, your secondary one. If you're not engaged in any business with the faculty, you can use this as your workplace, even redirect visitors your way. Go ahead, use the card the registrar gave you."

"Ah. Right."

[/list]

Cui walked up to the door and slid the card down the reader, and after a second it unlocked, sliding down and revealing the outer yard, leading into the southern hall of the siheyuan. It was as she had stated. Inside was not an open living room with its rows of couches and televisions screens, but instead a utilitarian lobby. A long carpet graces the entrance, then a few tables and chairs for guests, as the south hall was for visits and appointments.

No business was being undertaken yet within the hall, as it was still the beginning of the new semester, and so Zhang opted to sit at one of the tables and waited for Cui to settle down as well. Apart from a few Red Guards that were seen occasionally patrolling the vicinity of the site, it doesn't seem like anyone was planning on interrupting their privacy for now.

[list]

"So..." Cui began, tapping away his fingers on the table in boredom. "You dragged me to my new office to talk about that then?"

"Mhm." Zhang responds, nodding quietly. "As party secretary, you'll be the new face of our university, Comrade Cui. Anything you do will be representative of the Min Zhu Party, and anything the Min Zhu Party does is representative of the Qianxun nation."

"Seems like a heavy job. So what am I supposed to not do then?"

"A man of your and stature should know what must not be done, Comrade Cui."

"And the things I must do?"

"..."

[/list]

Zhang quieted for a second, her hands moving to her glasses which she adjusts upwards as she turned and reached for her large handbag, planting it firmly on the table. Out of it, she pulled out a yellow plastic blinder and opened to a specific page, then pushing the binder over to Cui. However, before he could get a good look, Zhang covers the documents with her hand, her countenance on the razor edge between wariness and fear.

[list]

"Before that." She said. "I want to ask if you really are close with the General Secretary."

"I'm not." Cui clarified, answering almost instantly. "Is it serious?"

"... It's... going to be the main thing we'll be turning to you for as our party secretary..." Zhang admits, retreating her hand. "Get a good look at the binder, Comrade Cui. There's been strange things happening at Qianxun Major. Students have been walking around the place at night, especially on full moons, like they're in a trance..."

"Huh. That's... odd?..."

[/list]

Cui quickly glosses over the binder. It was news reports, many of them headlining exactly what Zhang had just described. Students, roused in their sleep by a strange presence or emanation, then walking towards the lake in search of something. It seemed bizarre at first, perhaps ultimately innocuous, but as Cui turned the pages of the binder, the reports became grimmer and grimmer. Distant photographs turned into hospitalization reports, then into obituary photographs. Memorials began appearing, death certificates, even grim satirical cartoons, but only for a short while before disappearing, likely suppressed for vulgarity.

[list]

"They're walking into the lake?" Cui mouthed out, exasperated by what he had just read.

"And not coming back up." Zhang added. "No bodies or anything. We've been investigating this lake for sixty years, Comrade Cui. Humans can't go past the thermocline on their own, and all of a sudden we're having intelligent men and woman walking to their deaths, with no traces of where they ended up."

"Why didn't yo-..."

"Ask the General Secretary? He told us to keep it under wraps." Zhang says, crestfallen. "Says we couldn't risk damaging the reputation of the university. We couldn't even install any barriers since they said it would interfere with research. Which is why we're hoping you'd help, Comrade Cui. I know why you ended up here, but the most you can make out of it now is to help us solve this mess. It's been going on for months, and we can't understand why."

"... Does the Directorate know about this?" Cui asked.

"The Directorate is run by your uncle's friends, Comrade Cui. This is why we turn to you for help."

"... This is a lot you're springing to me on my first day, Comrade Zhang... give me some time to think about it..."

"Very well, Comrade Cui." Zhang replied, sighing as she leaned over to grab her binder, placing it neatly back into her handbag. Then, standing up, she turned to unlock the front door of the siheyuan herself. Before she left, she would turn around one more time with some parting remarks to Cui. "I'll leave you the rest of the day to explore your office. Meet me tomorrow at the Registrar, the Almstedts want to meet with you too. I'll see you later, Comrade Cui."

[/list]

Then, she departed, leaving Cui alone for the time being. In that silence, a strange song hummed but could not be heard.

Think of it like this
The Grand Council (or Grand Parliament)

This would be the central legislative body for the Grand Empire.

Structure: Instead of a single body, you could have two houses to represent different interests:

The Chamber of Nations: This house would have an equal number of representatives from each of the three member nations, regardless of their size or population. This ensures the smaller nations (Camphill and Clarentine) have an equal say and their sovereignty is protected.

The Assembly of Citizens: This house would have representatives based on the population of each nation. This would give Akhratia, as the larger nation, a greater voice on matters that affect the general population.

Powers: The Grand Council would only have authority over specific, pre-agreed-upon matters, such as:

Foreign Policy: Representing the Grand Empire in international relations.

Defense: Maintaining a joint military force or coordinating defense strategies.

Trade and Currency: Regulating trade between the member nations and potentially managing a shared currency.

Grand Imperial Law: Legislation that supersedes national law in specific, limited areas.

2. National Governments (Akhratia, Camphill, and Clarentine)

These would remain the primary governments for their respective nations.

Powers: They would retain full authority over domestic affairs, including:

Internal Laws: Civil, criminal, and cultural laws.

Taxation: Collecting taxes from their citizens.

Social Services: Healthcare, education, and social welfare programs.

Justice System: National courts and law enforcement.

3. The Royal Family of Akhratia

You mentioned the Camphillians have married into the Akhratian royal family. This is a great political tool.

Role of the Monarch: The Akhratian monarch could be the ceremonial Head of the Grand Empire. Their role would be to symbolize unity, but they would have limited political power. Think of them like the British monarch's role in the Commonwealth.

The "Union" with Camphill: The marriage could create a special status for Camphill. Maybe their head of state is a member of the Akhratian royal family, but they still have their own government. This makes Camphill a "personal union" with Akhratia, but not a fully integrated state. This explains why they are more intertwined than Clarentine.

4. The Status of Clarentine

As a former part of Akhratia, Clarentine's relationship is different.

Special Privileges: Clarentine might have some unique privileges or treaties from the time of its separation. For example, they could have guaranteed representation in the Grand Council or specific trade agreements. This acknowledges their shared history while affirming their current independence.

The "Commonwealth" Aspect: Clarentine's relationship with the Grand Empire could be more like a traditional commonwealth membera sovereign nation that voluntarily participates in the union for mutual benefit, particularly in defense or trade.
